release_levels.label: Engineering preflight
release_levels.allowed_claim: Series identity and coarse review candidates only

release_levels.label: Production image QC
release_levels.allowed_claim: Reviewed usable-tissue denominator; no lesion endpoint

release_levels.label: Reviewer-gated section analysis
release_levels.allowed_claim: Section-level quantitative and blinded ordinal results

release_levels.label: Confirmatory mouse reporting
release_levels.allowed_claim: Prespecified mouse-level endpoints in an adequately designed cohort

release_levels.label: Multimodal G-SURF association
release_levels.allowed_claim: Mouse-level H&E-to-IF association; spatial transfer only after registration validation

features.name: QuPath project and deterministic slide inventory
features.implementation: Create one versioned QuPath project entry per declared analytical series; resolve source, series, mouse, slide and section only from the study profile; reject extra, missing, thumbnail or uncalibrated series.
acceptance: The current study resolves exactly four mice and eight analytical sections.
A renamed, missing or extra series produces a blocking error rather than a guess.
Every output row carries stable mouse, slide, section and source-series identity.
features.remaining_blocker: The pilot opens declared series directly but does not create a persistent QuPath project or reusable inventory table.

features.name: Frozen acquisition-batch H&E stain profile
features.implementation: Estimate background RGB and hematoxylin/eosin vectors from small reviewed representative regions, exclude unrecognized colors, review separated channels, then freeze one named and hashed profile for the acquisition batch. Never estimate per condition or per slide during confirmatory analysis.
acceptance: A reviewer signs off hematoxylin, eosin and residual-channel separation across all sections.
The batch runner consumes the frozen profile and records its SHA-256.
Any missing or different profile blocks R2 and R3 output.
features.remaining_blocker: The pilot uses provisional hard-coded vectors.

features.name: Scan-quality and artifact exclusion
features.implementation: Generate distinct masks for pen, coverslip/background, dust, dark saturation, folds, tears, bubbles and focus/blur failure. Keep automatic exclusions separate from review-only candidates and preserve the original plus overlay for every section.
acceptance: Every excluded pixel has one reason code and is visible in a QC overlay.
Mask areas reconcile with detected tissue and usable tissue within one classification pixel.
A blinded holdout audit reports class-wise false exclusions and missed artifacts before profile lock.
features.remaining_blocker: Only red-pen candidates are automatically excluded; dark regions are review-only and fold, tear, blur, dust and bubble handling are not implemented.

features.name: Validated usable-tissue mask
features.implementation: Replace the coarse OD-sum rule with a saved QuPath thresholder or compact pixel classifier trained from small, diverse annotations across all mice. Use Tissue, Glass and Ignore* classes and create cleaned tissue objects with prespecified hole and fragment rules.
acceptance: Training, tuning and locked audit regions are separated at mouse or slide level.
Accuracy is reported against blinded point annotations and area masks, stratified by section and artifact class.
Low tissue coverage, denominator mismatch or classifier/profile drift blocks downstream endpoints.
features.remaining_blocker: The current downsample-64 OD threshold is suitable only for overview review.

features.name: Anatomical compartment map
features.implementation: Use reviewer annotations plus a compact multi-scale pixel/object classifier to map airway, vessel, alveolar parenchyma, pleura and Unresolved. Derive peribronchial and perivascular rings from reviewed structure boundaries rather than color alone.
acceptance: Airway and vessel boundaries are audited on a locked set spanning normal, infected and artifact-rich tissue.
Uncertain geography is emitted as Unresolved and never converted to a negative lesion call.
Boundary lengths and reference areas are exported in calibrated physical units.
features.remaining_blocker: No H4 classifier, anatomy objects or reviewed boundary-length denominator exists.

features.name: Nuclear detection and cellularity density
features.implementation: Run QuPath hematoxylin/OD-sum nuclear detection only inside usable tissue at a locked resolution. Tune on small ROIs representing normal alveoli, consolidation, airway, vessel and artifacts; preserve detections for point-based correction and audit.
acceptance: A blinded point-count audit reports count bias and precision by compartment and section.
Merged, fragmented and missed nuclei failure modes are documented and within a prespecified project tolerance.
The output is labelled cellularity, never immune-cell lineage.
features.remaining_blocker: The pilot measures dense hematoxylin pixels, not nuclei.

features.name: PR8 injury candidate maps
features.implementation: Train section-level candidates from multi-scale hematoxylin/eosin, texture, cellularity and airspace features for alveolar/interstitial inflammation, consolidation, peribronchial cuff, perivascular cuff and epithelial injury/debris. Keep edema, hemorrhage and necrosis as separate reviewed labels when visually distinguishable.
acceptance: Annotations are small, diverse, approximately balanced and drawn from multiple mice and sections.
Classifier development never uses genotype or infection labels as image features.
Performance is reported per lesion class on a locked holdout set; pseudo-probability is not called calibrated probability.
features.remaining_blocker: Dense-hematoxylin thresholding cannot distinguish inflammatory geography, collapse, edema, necrosis or airway injury.

features.name: Morphology and topology authorization
features.implementation: Apply explicit rules to candidate objects: cuff candidates must contact the appropriate reviewed boundary and form a surrounding band; alveolar lesions must lie in alveolar reference space; airway injury/debris must be epithelial or luminal. Route conflicts and low-confidence objects to Indeterminate.
acceptance: Every accepted or rejected candidate records the compartment, topology checks and decision reason.
Candidates in incompatible or unresolved anatomy cannot become positive calls.
Rule behavior is covered by synthetic geometry tests and a locked reviewed WSI audit.
features.remaining_blocker: No topology engine or authorized lesion object exists.

features.name: Blinded review and ordinal pathology rubric
features.implementation: Create a label-blinded review queue covering every mouse and both sections. Support accept, edit, reject and Indeterminate for masks, plus locked 0-4 rubrics for alveolitis/interstitial inflammation, bronchiolitis/epithelial injury, peribronchial cuffing, perivascular cuffing and consolidation. Preserve original and edited geometry.
acceptance: Reviewer cannot see genotype, infection or IF endpoint values during primary review.
Rubric anchors define extent and severity separately and include representative examples.
Intra-reviewer repeat and, when available, inter-reviewer agreement are reported before rubric lock.
Unreviewed required objects block R2 and higher outputs.
features.remaining_blocker: The locked whole-section rubric, blinded package, strict review parser and audit-last aggregation gate exist, but all eight current section rows still require accepted biological review; geometry-edit provenance remains future work for mask-based endpoints.

features.name: Section metrics and technical-repeatability QC
features.implementation: Export calibrated section numerators and denominators for every endpoint. Compare BF_01 with BF_02 as technical sections using paired difference plots, absolute and relative difference and an agreement statistic chosen before inspection.
acceptance: Each fraction can be recomputed exactly from exported numerator and denominator.
Technical sections never increase biological n.
Repeatability limits are established on a larger development cohort before confirmatory use.
features.remaining_blocker: The ordinal path retains paired technical-section values, minimum/maximum and exact agreement without inventing a composite. Quantitative H5-H6 endpoints and larger-cohort repeatability limits still require labelled development and validation.

features.name: Fail-closed section-to-mouse aggregation
features.implementation: Verify the expected section set, QC and review state, then pool raw numerators and denominators within mouse. Retain section rows and prespecify the ordinal mouse summary. Emit no mouse result when a required section or review is missing.
acceptance: Mouse fractions equal sum(section numerators) divided by sum(section denominators).
Incomplete, duplicate or mismatched section identity fails closed.
The current four-mouse cohort remains descriptive and cannot emit group hypothesis tests.
features.remaining_blocker: The strict ordinal section-to-mouse engine exists and publishes nothing for an incomplete or invalid review. Current biological review is incomplete, and future quantitative fractions still require validated H5-H6 numerators and denominators.

features.name: Mouse-level H&E to IF association
features.implementation: Join prespecified H&E injury endpoints to confocal KRT5 pod and AT1/AT2-state endpoints by canonical mouse identity. Preserve modality-specific QC and analyze associations only in an adequately powered biological cohort.
acceptance: The join is one row per mouse and rejects ambiguous or missing sample identity.
No cell- or region-level spatial transfer is performed without a separate registration-validation record.
Endpoints, exclusions and models are prespecified before confirmatory group labels are opened.
features.remaining_blocker: The present cohort has one mouse per genotype-by-infection cell and no validated serial-section registration.

features.name: Launcher Route 3 workflow
features.implementation: Add a dedicated H&E screen with study profile, QuPath path, source folder, fresh output, stain profile, run tier and review/resume controls. Expose R0/R1 engineering operation before R2/R3, but keep biological reporting unavailable until all release gates pass.
acceptance: Route 3 never calls the fluorescence Fiji engine.
The launcher displays the highest authorized release level and allowed claim before execution.
Missing profiles, validation records, review decisions or cohort eligibility block the corresponding tier.
A launcher self-test proves that changing BrightfieldRouteEnabled alone cannot bypass the gates.
features.remaining_blocker: Route 3 is intentionally disabled and has no production runner or review workflow.

features.name: Validation, provenance and reporting package
features.implementation: Hash configuration, scripts, classifiers and stain profiles; record QuPath and reader versions, calibrated resolution, source identity, exclusions, reviewer actions and run tier. Keep development, tuning and locked validation sets separate at mouse/slide level and report all failures.
acceptance: Every result is traceable to immutable inputs, code, profile and review state.
No patch or section from one mouse appears in both development and locked validation partitions.
The report states experimental unit, exclusions, blinding, sample-size basis and uncertainty.
Automation performance is reported by section and mouse, not only as pooled pixels.
features.remaining_blocker: Exact raw VSI packages, R1/H4 packages, the locked rubric and H7/H8 output audit are content-bound. H5-H6 classifier partitions, completed reviewer evidence and locked biological validation reports do not yet exist.

non_goals: Inferring immune lineage from H&E morphology alone
Calling color-deconvolution intensity a quantitative stain-concentration endpoint
Inferring alveolar number or volume from ordinary two-dimensional profiles
Treating technical sections as independent mice
Fully automated pathology grading without pathologist-labelled development and independent validation
